texts.title: A Day at Sultanhanı
texts.body:
Last spring, my class went on a school trip to Sultanhanı. It is a small town near Aksaray, in the middle of Turkey. There is a very old caravanserai there. The Seljuk sultan Alaeddin Keykubad built it in 1229, so it is almost 800 years old.

A caravanserai was a kind of hotel for travelers. In the past, merchants traveled with camels and carried silk, spices and other goods. Every evening they needed a safe place to sleep. They stopped at a caravanserai, and their animals rested there too.

When we arrived, our teacher showed us the big stone gate. It was taller than my house! Inside, there was a large courtyard with a small mosque in the middle. Then we walked into a long, dark hall. It was cold inside, but it was very quiet and beautiful.

I took a lot of photos. My favorite part was the gate because it had beautiful stone patterns. Next year, I am going to visit another caravanserai with my family.

texts.title: Riverside Library: Story Club
texts.body:
RIVERSIDE LIBRARY
Story Club for Young Readers

Do you like stories? Come and join our Story Club!

When: Every Saturday, from 10:00 to 11:30
Where: Room 3, second floor
Age: 12–15
Cost: Free

At the club, we read a short story in English together. Then we talk about it and play word games. In the last week of every month, each member tells a story to the group.

What to bring: a notebook and a pen. You do not need to bring a book. The library gives you the stories.

How to join: Write your name on the list at the information desk. Please join before 1 November. There are only 20 places.

The club starts on 8 November.
